geography.why: Double Underweight, carried unchanged on this week's reading. Goldman Sachs (16 Oct) has French spreads at decade highs with tentative spillover to Italy and judges France's fiscal challenge 'harder now than in 2011-15'; the premium in basis points was not read, so the reversal conditions (back to D under 120 basis points, to C under 100) could not be tested and are plainly not met at a decade high. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country; no live holding is French-listed. Counter-case unchanged: a country letter is a blunt tool on 110 stocks and lands on French-listed global businesses (TotalEnergies, whose memo exposures lift its Thematic Fit/Momentum by two grades through the stock layer; Soitec; Sopra Steria; Alten) as hard as on domestic banks and property; and Goldman's own judgement is that disorderly escalation is less likely than in 2011-15.

memo.verdict: Park at Triaging, conviction medium. Not progressing at this pass. Reassessment conditions: (1) a Business Foundation report closes the current single-report research gap (particularly management-incentive alignment and margin-structure detail); (2) at least one further quarterly print confirms the March 2026 order-book recovery (1.00% organic growth) is converting into delivered positive organic revenue growth, not merely a stabilised order book; (3) the FY26 guidance range (2%-3% organic growth) holds through at least two quarters without revision, breaking the two-year serial-guidance-cut pattern. Two downstream actions: (1) brief the Chief of Staff to generate the Business Foundation report for IPS-FR, front-of-queue, since this is the thinnest-sourced memo in the current batch; (2) calendar a reassessment trigger review at the Q2 2026 print (expected late July/August 2026) testing organic growth delivery against FY26 guidance and the SSEM momentum reading for improvement off the current F. Watchlist placement retained under Viewforth sector tag K.5, flagged for the valuation anchor (6.30x forward P/E, 8th percentile) and the reassessment triggers, not for imminent progression. What would most efficiently accelerate reassessment ahead of Q2: (a) the dashboard-sourced SSEM grade moving off F, or (b) management itself narrowing the six named key drivers to two or three treated as primary.
case: The memo's own case for staying interested, in its logical order: (1) Internal change is the strongest single positive in the memo — a complete leadership reset within twelve months (CEO Sept-25, CFO Dec-25, board chair Mar-26, chief platforms/technology officer Feb-26, new independent advisory board chair May-26), paired with the Horizons roadmap targeting 3-4% average organic growth for 2026-2028 and operating margin expansion to 13.5% by 2028 (5%+ growth and 14%+ margin by 2030). (2) The order book returned to 1.00% organic growth in March 2026, driven by a Public Affairs rebound after an 8.00% organic decline through FY25; Globally Managed Services is targeted to add several hundred million euros to the revenue base through double-digit growth. (3) Regulatory tailwind: tightening data-privacy regulation (GDPR, CCPA, evolving US state laws) is explicitly framed by directors as favouring scaled, compliant players like Ipsos over smaller panel operators. (4) Valuation is the one clean positive: 6.30x forward P/E sits at the 8th percentile of the stock's own ten-year history; Bernstein's EUR 73 target (blending EUR 65 historical-multiple and EUR 81 DCF valuations) and the EUR 55.3 broader consensus both sit well above the EUR 36.2 live price. KT&Partners values comparable lower-growth research operators around 0.80x EV/Sales and 5.00x EV/EBITDA. (5) Balance sheet discipline is genuine: 0.50x net debt/EBITDA against a 2.0x ceiling, dividend and buyback maintained through the transition, enterprise client retention on accounts above EUR 1m over 99%. (6) Ipsos Facto, a proprietary generative AI platform launched July 2023 ahead of most peers, is a credible internal productivity tool automating coding, translation and report drafting, positioned to meet client demand for sub-48-hour turnarounds. (7) Panel-quality management is a demonstrated operational strength: multi-factor authentication cut suspicious recruits 50%, and Ipsos India's Total Access gives consolidated access to 3.5 million panel members. (8) Custom, complex research remains defensible against automated competitors per expert-call evidence, in explicit contrast to the automated tracking work being lost to YouGov. Despite this, the memo concludes the tests failed outnumber the one test passed, and recommends Park.
counter_case: No separate Risks report exists for this stock (Change Forces is the sole source on disk), so the counter-case is the memo's own carried opposing arguments, preserved at full strength:

Sell-side earnings momentum is data-pinned F: every revision horizon from one to twelve months is negative (EPS revisions of negative 2%, 1%, 3%, 5% across one/three/six/twelve months, composite momentum score negative 15) — the single most negative data point in the whole memo, sourced directly from the Master Dashboard bell-curve SSEM value, not from Watson's own reading, removing subjective judgement from the park decision.
triggers: The Business Foundation report is the single highest-priority research gap: it must close the current single-report reliance (Change Forces only), particularly on management-incentive alignment (E8.RA6 CQ8 — executive compensation linkage to Horizons targets not disclosed in the source material) and margin-structure detail underlying the E8.RA4/RA5/RA6 quality caveats and the E11 competitive-intensity read. At least one further quarterly print must confirm the March 2026 order-book recovery (1.00% organic growth) is converting into delivered positive organic revenue growth, not merely a stabilised order book — tracked specifically at the Q2 2026 print (expected late July/August 2026). The FY26 guidance range (2%-3% organic growth) must hold through at least two quarters without revision, breaking the two-year serial-guidance-cut pattern named in E8.RA7. Two developments together would justify an accelerated reassessment ahead of the standard Q2 trigger: (a) the dashboard-sourced SSEM grade moving off F, evidencing the sell-side pricing in the Horizons roadmap rather than continuing to cut estimates; (b) management itself narrowing the six named key drivers to two or three treated as primary, which would directly flip the E7.RA1 guardrail finding. Additional named tests: whether the FY26 guidance range holds without revision through two consecutive quarters would move E7.RA5 from C toward B; whether the healthcare vertical's 500-expert, 40-country scale is defensible against IQVIA with quantified market-share evidence versus a qualitative retention claim; whether the Business Foundation report's margin-trend data shows the gap to subscription-platform peers narrowing (evidence against the false-friend read under E8.RA8) or holding flat/widening (evidence for it); tracking YouGov's next reporting cycle for further brand-tracking share-loss evidence. The Iran-thematic input (E5.RA3) is flagged stale (last refreshed over four months prior in Richard's March 2026 journal entries) and was assessed on Watson's own judgement rather than the suspended `memory/thematics/active.md` file; E5 should be re-run at Early-Stage Assessment once that file is refreshed, and Richard should be flagged directly that the Iran-thematic screen could not be tested against fresh guidance. Client-level concentration data for Ipsos.Digital specifically was not surfaced (flagged as a Business Foundation research gap), and a self-initiated research angle on Kantar's private financials was considered but not pursued since Kantar is Bain Capital-owned and comparable disclosed financials are not reliably available.
